precepts.text: Though we preach the gospel, we have nothing to glory of, cuz all the glory goes back to the father. Necessity is laid upon each and every one of us to go out there and wake our people up so they can repent. Woe is unto us if we preach not the gospel. We got to do this thing willingly; nobody can force you. If you do it willingly, you have a reward: a crown, everlasting life, immortality. But if against your will, he going to take his spirit from you, and you will find yourself back outside them doors in the midst of wickedness again.
precepts.point: And now we be here praying for you.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
The prayer is that God would “give you all an heart to serve him, and to do his will, with a good courage and a willing mind.” If you want to return, if you want to repent, he will give you a heart to serve him and to keep his law and commandments. And it must be with a willing mind. Paul shows what that means.

“For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of”: though we preach the gospel, we have nothing to glory of, because all the glory goes back to the Father. “For necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Necessity is laid upon each and every one of us to go out there and wake our people up, so they can repent, come out of it, and cast away their iniquities. Woe unto us if we preach not the gospel.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” We have to do this thing willingly. Nobody can force you. If you do it willingly you have a reward: a crown, everlasting life, immortality. “But if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.” If you do it against your will, he will take his spirit from you, and you will find yourself back outside those doors in the midst of wickedness and evil again.

So we have to serve the Lord with a willing mind, a sincere heart, and loyalty. We have to come out of all the wickedness we learned here in America, from under the hypnosis given to us here, and serve him willingly.

precepts.text: I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: that is the dying daily. Lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway. Paul knew he would drift if he did not die daily and give life to the spiritual man daily.
precepts.point: I die daily. Paul is talking about that same daily: you starve the carnal man and feed the spiritual man.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ said, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.” There is that daily again. Paul says it of himself: “I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.” How do you do it? By feeding. You deny the carnal man and feed the spiritual man. Not that you stop eating; you starve the carnal and feed the spiritual.

Paul shows it in chapter 9: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”. That is the dying daily. “lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway”. Paul preached to others, but he knew he would drift if he did not die daily and give life to the spiritual man daily as well.

Romans says the same: “if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.” You cannot do that without constant connection to the scriptures. Many say they are battling depression or sin, but they do not open their Bible every day; they are not battling anything. When somebody with good works and a good reputation moves to the left or the right, it is because they stopped feeding themselves daily. That is scary; we all have to check ourselves.

There is no excuse anymore: you have a Bible with you all the time, on your phone. The pattern runs through the whole book: daily bread, daily mercy, take up your cross daily, daily death, daily renewal. “though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day”. The outward man dies; the inward man must be fed. That is daily bread for a dying man.

precepts.text: For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope, and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.
precepts.point: His God doth instruct him to discretion. Discreet means careful and circumspect in speech or action, to avoid causing offence or to gain an advantage. Learn discernment: how to speak and when to speak, which someone should tell our wives, in order to win souls.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
Isaiah gives an analogy of a farmer: “Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground?” He breaks the dirt, makes the ground flat, and casts abroad his seeds. But is Isaiah really talking about farmland?

Paul answers it: “Or saith he it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope; and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.” It wasn't really talking about farms. The plowing and the threshing were not about growing seeds.

The plowing represents teaching. We are to plow in hope: to teach, instruct, and give hope to our people. You brothers are fishers of men, and the field is our people. That is how Isaiah 28 applies to you.

So the fitches, cummin, principal wheat, appointed barley and rye are the different people we plow for, and the farmer's instruments are the different ways we must deal with them to persuade them to salvation. By long forbearing even a prince is persuaded, and Israel is a prince: we have to be patient with our people.

precepts.text: I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection, lest when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway. You can control your sexual appetite by controlling your food intake: abstain from the foods you desire and are tempted with. Alcohol is stored in your brain with late nights and social gatherings, so refuse to drink in that environment and you tell your reward vectors who is in charge. Abstain from the candy you love, and you gain power over the things with more control over you. Then disconnect the feelings associated with pornography, Instagram, and looking, rewire the neurons, and fire them into a new habit, open a Bible instead, so the brain associates that environment with the new function.
precepts.point: I realized I actually have a lust for food: the jelly donut at Dunkin', the Doritos, thoughts replaying something you desire but are not supposed to have, until you justify one cookie and give in. That is no different from pornography, adultery, or fornication. And it is a big deal, because if you are not in the green you cannot go on the street; the Lord is putting a cap on us to show it is the exact same battle, a worldly lust inherited through America.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
Peter says to “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the two biggest fleshly lusts in the world, going back to Genesis, are food and sex: one deals with nourishing and one with procreation. Paul shows how to fight that war: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” The whole purpose is to bring our body into subjection, in what we take in through our mouth and what we take in through our eyes.

One way to keep your body in subjection: you can control your sexual appetite and your lust by controlling your food intake. The foods you desire, the foods you like, the foods you are tempted with, practice abstaining from them. Take alcohol. The brain stores alcohol with a time and an environment: late at night, social gatherings, partying, celebrating. So brothers that watch porn, try not drinking when everybody around you is drinking. If you can abstain from that, you can abstain from anything else. You are telling your flesh and your reward vectors, even though my brain says drink in this environment, I am going against what my body wants.

Or the candy you love: abstain from it. If you can abstain from the things you love, you gain control and power over the things that have even more control and power over you. You are training your body and your mind and disassociating things from it until you have full control over your vessel.

Then when it comes to sexual temptation, you tell your body, no, I am not associating this feeling with pornography, this feeling with Instagram, this feeling with looking. Disconnect that association, rewire the neurons, and fire them into a different, positive behavior. When you go into that environment, open up a Bible, do something else, and train your brain to associate that feeling with the new habit. There is a way to get complete control over it, so that having preached to others, you yourself are not a castaway.

precepts.text: Unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; that is why Paul took the charges of the vow.
precepts.point: The elders at Jerusalem told Paul to purify himself with four men which had a vow on them and be at charges with them, that all may know thou thyself walkest orderly and keepest the law. And note it well: the thousands there that believed were Jews, all zealous of the law, and the Gentiles Paul taught among were Jews scattered among the Gentiles.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
When a Nazarite’s separation was defiled by the dead, he shaved his head on the seventh day, brought two turtles or two young pigeons on the eighth day and a lamb of the first year for a trespass offering, and the days before were lost. Paul partook in that Nazarite purification.

“And unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; to them that are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain them that are under the law.”

Unto the Jews he became a Jew; he brought himself down to their level of understanding to win them over, not by breaking the law but by walking orderly and keeping it. That is why Paul took the charges of the vow.

precepts.point: Paul warns in 1 Corinthians 9:27 that he keeps his body under subjection lest he himself become a castaway.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Paul himself did not take his standing for granted: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.”

If Titus, an elder of the highest rank, could be drawn away by the false brethren, then even the one who preached to others could become a castaway. Paul kept his body under subjection because of it.

precepts.point: Eventually, if you are not of the elect, it will be manifest in your spirit and you will leave. The same thing happened in the apostles' time is happening today under different names but the same spirits.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.”

The false brethren who went out from among the disciples were made manifest that they were not of us. Paul, who preached to others, kept his body under subjection so that he would not be a castaway. You cannot fake this truth forever; the one who does not keep himself under will be made manifest and leave.

Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway. So you can be a teacher, a preacher to others, an instructor and wisdom to others, but it is unprofitable to yourself. Paul said, in dealing with the Corinthians, I do not want to be a castaway. So therefore, not only do I have to teach this to you, but I have to live it as well. Otherwise he is unprofitable to himself, like we just read in Sirach 37. And we cannot have that.

Bitterness. We are in denial. We are in denial until there is a breaking of the breach or the wall, and just an overflow like Hurricane Katrina coming through. You are like, how did I end up here? You did not deal with it when it was little building blocks and little nuances. You did not deal with it. You did not say anything. You acted like everything was normal.

For though I preach the gospel: everybody, all you brothers, you preach the gospel; you sisters, you got kids, you preaching the gospel to them. For necessity is laid upon me: we want to save our lives, we want the coming Jerusalem. Yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

points: For if I do this thing willingly: if you do this thing willing, you have a passion for this truth, loyalty to God Almighty, and I have a reward. But if against my will: if somebody always got to yell at me, tell me to do this and do that, because I'm a hireling, I'm really not in this thing; you don't hear how boring I am, I got a dead spirit on me, I could care less.

A dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me: you get a limited amount of time in this truth, and then God moves you out the way and brings somebody else. That's musical chairs. We've seen it over the years: it's like whole new congregations that come before us; same spirits, but it's a different people. On your phone it says memories on Facebook, it'll go back two years, and I'm like, who's these brothers I was standing with? And it's all new people, because them dudes fell out.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

points: I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air. This truth is a fight: against the sins of the world and the sins in yourself.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway. Even Paul had to fight himself all the time. We all have a battle in us; so we cannot sit and say, he is condemned, while doing the same or worse. And the one who leaves and stays gone, the Bible calls a castaway if he stays that way.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: The fight is not physical; the fight is spiritual, meaning it is in your mind. Every sin that every last one of us commits starts in the mind. If you can kill it there, it will not manifest itself. If you kill the root of bitterness in your mind when that seed tries creeping in, it is not going to bear a root.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: So fight I, not as one that beateth the air: fighting Satan is not swinging in the air. But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: the way you fight Satan is controlling your body and controlling your mind.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Though I preach the gospel I have nothing to glory of, for necessity is laid upon me; woe is unto me if I preach not. Paul knew he was a servant sent to deliver souls. Destruction unto me if I do not do what I was sent to do. What have you done since you came to IUIC besides show up on Sabbath? Some of you only pick up the Bible on Saturday, because you cannot answer a simple question.

If I do this thing willingly I have a reward, but if against my will, a dispensation is committed unto me. Do it willingly, not because a deacon says it; after two weeks of being told, you slide back, which shows it was forced. Little brothers in purple, never force a brother to sweep the floor; if he says no, get another brother and move on, because forced work has no spirit in it.

You force yourself to come every Sabbath as a burden, yet you willingly get up at four to give the white man eight or twelve hours in pain without a day off. You love the master. Which is more important, the kingdom that has no end or the master's job? America turns 250 this July.

What is my reward? That I preach the gospel without charge. Though free from all men, I made myself servant unto all. Bishop Nathanyel is a servant, Bishop Yawasap is a servant, Bishop Canaan is a servant, the deacons are servants; we are here to serve the people and build you up for what is coming.
